To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the health system functions most relevant to the success of priority health programs in maternal health, as perceived by different categories of actors, are hospital infrastructure, human resource training, health policy and program development.

the health system functions most important to decision makers in maternal health are: hospital infrastructure and human resource capacity; health policy; program development; intercultural and social participation; social networks.

(1) the health system functions identified by the actors are those of the health care system and of health care delivery, with a focus on the health care infrastructure and on the human resource training and management; (2) health policy is a function that is not clearly defined by the actors; (3) program development, inter-cultural and community participation and the social networks are functions that are clearly stated but less focused and with a lower perceived importance; (4) the functions are not equally perceived as
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: What health system functions are considered most critical by key stakeholders to improve maternal health in Mexico?
the identification of health system functions that are important for the delivery of priority health programs and the analysis of these functions from a systems perspective.
the development of a framework for the identification of critical maternal health system functions and the mapping of these functions in different contexts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the concept mapping approach can be used to identify critical functions constituting an adaptive health system, including aspects of actors' perspectives that are not included in normative or analytical frameworks.
health system functions are not the same for all actors and that the differences in the way they perceive them can be used to strengthen health system performance.
health system functions are not static, but dynamic constructs that are subject to continuous evolution, depending on the actors' perceptions of what is important and feasible for their work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
health system strengthening should include not only health sector functions but also the social context, given structures as well as manageable processes.

the concept mapping methodology can be useful to understand the health system from the perspective of actors in different levels and positions in the system, and to identify areas for capacity strengthening.
the health system functions identified are critical to ensure maternal health programs are integrated into the health system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of critical health system functions is a useful approach to strengthen health systems.
health systems are not only about structures, they are about processes as well.
a combination of normative, strategic and analytical frameworks and health system functions identified by critical actors is needed to strengthen maternal health systems.
